subject: Interaction of Observed Time variant and Time variant Observed variables [Growth Curve modelling]

messages.author: e60b4d9c1389d3d1
messages.subject: Interaction of Observed Time variant and Time variant Observed variables [Growth Curve modelling]
parts:
Hello all,

Just a quick question. How can I create an interaction of observed time variant and time invariant variables here? I want to create an interaction of Cluster [0/1] and Occupation: to see whether the effect of occupation on Y varies in the cluster; and also to see whether the difference in the growth of Y in cluster 1 vs cluster 0 is moderated by the occupation.

#Three-piece Growth Curve model

model.1 <-

'
Intercept =~ 1*Y1 + 1*Y2 + 1*Y3 + 1*Y4+ 1*Y5 + 1*Y6+ 1*Y7 + 1*Y8+ 1*Y9+ 1*Y10+ 1*Y11

Slope1 =~  (-3)*Y1 + (-2)*Y2 + (-1)*Y3 + 0*Y4+ 0*Y5 + 0*Y6+ 0*Y7 + 0*Y8+ 0*Y9+ 0*Y10+ 0*Y11
Slope2 =~  0*Y1 + 0*Y2 + 0*Y3 + 0*Y4+ 1*Y5 + 2*Y6+ 3*Y7 + 4*Y8+ 4*Y9+ 4*Y10+ 4*Y11
Slope3 =~  0*Y1 + 0*Y2 + 0*Y3 + 0*Y4+ 0*Y5 + 0*Y6+ 0*Y7 + 0*Y8+ 1*Y9+ 2*Y10+ 3*Y11

#Time-invariant covariate #cluster [1/0]

Intercept ~ Cluster  
Slope1 ~ Cluster 
Slope2 ~ Cluster  
Slope3 ~ Cluster  

#Time-variant covariate [Occupation 1/0]
Y1 ~ D1
Y2 ~ D2
Y3 ~ D3
Y4 ~ D4
Y5 ~ D5
Y6 ~ D6
Y7 ~ D7
Y8 ~ D8
Y9 ~ D9
Y10 ~ D10
Y11 ~ D11
 

' 

fit.1 <- growth(model.1, data=sem_data, estimator = "MLM")
summary(fit.1)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Interaction of Observed Time variant and Time variant Observed variables [Growth Curve modelling]
parts: How can I create an interaction of observed time variant and time invariant variables here? I want to create an interaction of Cluster [0/1] and Occupation: to see whether the effect of occupation on Y varies in the cluster; and also to see whether the difference in the growth of Y in cluster 1 vs cluster 0 is moderated by the occupation.

You need to add product terms to the regression equations.

Y1 ~ D1 + D1:Cluster

Cluster is a dummy code, so the slope of D1 is interpreted as its effect in Cluster 0, and the effect of the product term D1:Cluster is interpreted as how different that effect is in Cluster 1 than 0.

Because you are not constraining the effect of occupation on Y to equality over time, that effect is already moderated by time.  Likewise, without constraining the effect of product terms (D1:Cluster, D2:Cluster, ..., D9:Cluster) to equality over time, then the differences between their effects captures a 3-way interaction between time, cluster, and occupation.  You could start with that least restrictive specification, then test whether the effects over time can be constrained by giving them the same labels and

Y1 ~ foo*D1 + bar*D1:Cluster
Y2 ~ foo*D2 + bar*D2:Cluster

...
Y9 ~ foo*D9 + bar*D9:Cluster



Then comparing the models with a LRT using lavTestLRT() to see if the data show evidence against those constraints.  If you can't reject the H0, then you can just interpret the simpler 2-way interaction between Cluster and occupation. Otherwise, you have a more complicated interpretation to work through.

This recent tutorial might be informative:

https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2019.1627213
